title: A term QuickBooks already has under the same name is used and never changed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the test organization is connected to a QuickBooks Online sandbox company, and you can sign in to that company in another tab.
  • Make sure QuickBooks already has a term named term A, set as a standard term due in 20 days. In ShopView, term A is one of the shop's own terms, due 14 days after the invoice date. Customer A holds it and work order 1 for it is complete.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. On work order 1's Finance tab, set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  2. Click Create Invoice.
  3. Wait until the invoice has synced.
  4. In QuickBooks, open the Terms list (Settings, All lists, Terms).
  5. In QuickBooks, open the invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Due date reads Oct 19, 2026 (14 days, ShopView's rule).

Step 2:

  • The invoice is created.

Step 3:

  • The invoice is no longer on the QB Unexported report.

Step 4:

  • There is still one term A, still due in 20 days: ShopView did not change it or add a second one.

Step 5:

  • Its due date is Oct 19, 2026, the date ShopView sent (only the QuickBooks customer's term may differ).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11677 (Story 8, QuickBooks sync - credit terms)

  • S8-R4: “A term already in QuickBooks under the same name is used as it is; ShopView never changes a term in QuickBooks.”
  • S8-E1: “If QuickBooks already has a term with the same name but a different rule, QuickBooks keeps its own rule for that term (S8-R4). Each invoice still carries its own due date, so invoices stay correct; only the QuickBooks customer's term may differ.”
